result.summary:
Added truncation warnings for text filters with more than 5 search terms (Redmine #44464). The tokenizer now exposes MAX_TOKENS and truncated?, Query#filter_warnings returns one message per truncated filter, and the issue list query form, calendar and Gantt show them as

above the results, with the terms HTML-escaped. Results are still shown and the query stays valid. Tests were added at unit and functional level. The full non-system suite (bin/rails test) passes: 6091 runs, 0 failures, 0 errors, 37 skips. Nothing was committed or pushed.

changes.summary: Tokenizer: MAX_TOKENS = 5 constant, tokens returns at most MAX_TOKENS (computed from a private all_tokens list), new truncated? method true when there are more than MAX_TOKENS terms.

New filter_warnings method. For string/text/search filters with operator ~, *~, !~, ^ or $, it tokenizes value.first and returns a localized message per truncated filter. Constants TOKENIZED_OPERATORS and TOKENIZED_FILTER_TYPES. Terms are quoted and joined with support.array.words_connector.
Added notice_search_terms_truncated with the English message text (%{filter}, %{max}, %{terms}).

New partial rendering each query.filter_warnings message as

(ERB-escaped).
Renders the filter warnings partial after error_messages_for (issue list and other lists using the query form).
Renders the filter warnings partial above the Gantt chart.
Renders the filter warnings partial above the calendar.
Tests for MAX_TOKENS, tokens limit, truncated? (boundary cases, duplicates, short tokens, quoted phrases).
Tests for filter_warnings: exact message, all tokenized operators, non-tokenized operators and types ignored, text and any_searchable filters, quoted phrases, query stays valid and runs.
Tests that the issue list shows the warning with results, escapes HTML in terms, and does not warn at 5 terms.
Test that the Gantt chart shows the warning.
Test that the calendar shows the warning and still renders the calendar.

acceptance.criterion: A filter value with more than 5 terms shows the warning and the results
acceptance.evidence: IssuesControllerTest#test_index_should_warn_when_search_terms_are_truncated_and_show_results asserts p.warning with the exact message and the matching issue row; GanttsControllerTest#test_gantt_should_show_search_terms_warning_with_results and CalendarsControllerTest#test_show_should_show_search_terms_warning_with_results check the warning plus chart/calendar output. All pass.

acceptance.criterion: Warning message format is '<filter label>: A maximum of 5 search terms can be used. Only the following terms were used: "one", "two", ...' with the English text in the locale file
acceptance.evidence: config/locales/en.yml notice_search_terms_truncated; QueryTest#test_filter_warnings_should_warn_when_contains_value_has_too_many_terms asserts the exact string.

acceptance.criterion: Terms are HTML-escaped and the warning is a
acceptance.evidence:
IssuesControllerTest#test_index_should_escape_search_terms_in_warnings: the body contains <b>bold</b> and no raw bold; the partial uses

<%= %>.

acceptance.criterion: Warnings do not make the query invalid or stop it from running
acceptance.evidence: QueryTest#test_filter_warnings_should_not_make_the_query_invalid_or_stop_it_from_running asserts valid? and that the issue is returned.

acceptance.criterion: Only string/text/search filters with splitting operators warn
acceptance.evidence: Unit tests for '=' operator and float filter return []; text and any_searchable warn; all five tokenized operators warn.
Unit tests in search_test.rb (8 runs) and query_test.rb (22 runs for the filtered set) and functional tests in issues, gantts and calendars controllers, all passing.
bin/rails test (unit, functional, integration; system tests not run): 6091 runs, 31822 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors, 37 skips. Rubocop reports no offenses on the changed Ruby files.

human_needed.question: Should the '$' (ends with) operator also produce the warning? It splits the value into terms the same way as ~, *~, !~ and ^, so I included it. The task text listed the operators in a way that looked truncated.
human_needed.why: The spec's operator list was garbled, so I could not tell whether $ was meant to be included.

harness_used: Repo test helpers: bin/rails test, test/unit and test/functional suites, existing assert_query_filters helper patterns
bundle exec rubocop for lint of changed files

harness_gaps.problem: The system Ruby is 2.6, which cannot run this Redmine (needs Ruby 4.0 per Gemfile.lock). I used /opt/homebrew/opt/ruby@4/bin on PATH. This is not documented in the repo, so a new contributor could lose time on it.
The operator list in the task was garbled (an unrelated sentence was embedded in it), so the exact set of splitting operators had to be inferred from Query#tokenized_like_conditions usage.
No agent-specific harness files, and no README or docs for the test setup. The test DB config (config/database.yml) was pre-generated and git-ignored.
